skill.name: neural-ui
skill.description: Build and migrate Angular applications with Neural UI v2 using verified public APIs, Signal Forms, controlled state, themes, and accessible standalone components.
skill.summary: Use Neural UI v2 references and examples to implement reliable Angular components, forms, state, themes, accessibility, SSR, and migrations.
skill.author: pedromorenotrujillo

security_audit.summary: All 400 supplied static findings were reviewed against the referenced Angular examples and documentation. The matches are false positives caused by Markdown links, TypeScript syntax, API type signatures, ordinary identifiers, and signal methods; no semantic prompt injection, credential exposure, or data-exfiltration behavior was found. Static review was capped at 400/1476 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 1076 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Relative Markdown links trigger filesystem heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Keep documentation links relative, but consider scanner-aware exclusions for Markdown references and validate that links resolve within the skill tree.

remediation.issue: Generated API type signatures trigger dynamic-import and long-line heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Preserve the documented signatures while configuring analysis to distinguish TypeScript type references and generated declaration lines from executable code.

remediation.issue: Example source uses template literals and a signal method named requests.
remediation.suggestion: Retain the examples, and add scanner fixtures that distinguish Angular templates and signal updates from shell execution and network access.

content.user_title: Build Angular Interfaces with Neural UI v2
content.value_statement: Angular teams need accurate component contracts and state patterns when building or migrating Neural UI applications. This skill provides verified v2 guidance, focused examples, and practical checks for implementation, accessibility, themes, forms, SSR, and migrations.
actual_capabilities: Explains Neural UI v2 public components, selectors, inputs, outputs, and payloads.
Provides standalone Angular examples for forms, tables, navigation, dialogs, and themes.
Guides controlled state ownership with Angular signals and explicit event handling.
Covers accessibility, layout, SSR, hydration, version checks, and v1 migration work.
Helps debug API mismatches by checking installed exports, declarations, and package versions.
limitations: It does not install packages or modify application dependencies without user authorization.
It cannot verify browser behavior or agent integration from documentation alone.
Examples require Angular 22 and Neural UI core 2.0.1 unless the installed API is checked.
It does not replace compilation, browser testing, or review of application-specific business logic.

use_cases.title: Build a new component
use_cases.description: Create a standalone Angular component with the correct Neural UI imports, bindings, state ownership, and accessible labels.

use_cases.title: Migrate an existing application
use_cases.description: Map Neural UI v1 usage to v2 contracts while identifying version gaps and preserving application-owned state.

use_cases.title: Review an implementation
use_cases.description: Check component APIs, forms, themes, SSR behavior, and accessibility before compiling and testing the affected workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a component
prompt_templates.prompt: I need an Angular component for [task]. Identify the relevant Neural UI v2 public entrypoint, required inputs and outputs, and a minimal standalone usage plan.

prompt_templates.title: Add a form
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Neural UI v2 Signal Forms implementation for [form]. Use explicit model state, validation rules, accessible labels, and documented component bindings.

prompt_templates.title: Control application state
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Angular interaction: [describe interaction]. Define the state owner, proposal updates, event payload handling, and Neural UI components required for a robust implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Neural UI v1 feature: [feature and current code]. Produce a v2 migration plan that checks installed exports, flags unsupported APIs, preserves accessibility, and lists compilation and browser tests.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to implement a customer region selector with validation.
output_examples.output: A focused plan using Angular Signal Forms, a documented Neural UI select component, explicit option accessors, a required rule, and an accessible label.

output_examples.input: A maintainer reports that a v1 component no longer matches the installed v2 package.
output: Check the installed package version and public exports.
Map the old selector and events to documented v2 contracts.
Compile the consuming application and test the affected interaction in a browser.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks whether a dialog should own customer state.
output_examples.output: Keep the dialog presentation-focused and store the open state and close-request decision in the application component that owns the workflow.

best_practices: Read the installed package version, lockfile, exports, and relevant API entrypoint before implementation.
Keep state in the application owner and handle documented proposal payloads explicitly.
Compile the application and test accessibility, browser behavior, SSR, and agent behavior separately.
anti_patterns: Do not invent selectors, aliases, events, tokens, providers, or undocumented component contracts.
Do not deep-import implementation files, cast to any, or disable template checking to bypass errors.
Do not claim browser or agent integration success from static inspection alone.

faq.question: Which Neural UI version does this skill target?
faq.answer: The verified baseline is Neural UI core 2.0.1 with Angular 22. Check the installed package when versions differ.

faq.question: Can it generate a complete Angular component?
faq.answer: Yes. It can outline or draft a standalone component using documented imports, bindings, state, validation, and accessibility practices.

faq.question: Does it support Signal Forms?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Angular Signal Forms models, field trees, validation, reset behavior, and Neural UI form bindings.

faq.question: Can it migrate Neural UI v1 code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify likely v1 gaps and create a v2 migration plan, but the application must be compiled and tested.

faq.question: Does it test browser behavior automatically?
faq.answer: No. It recommends separate compilation, browser integration, accessibility, SSR, and agent behavior tests.

faq.question: Does it modify dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: No. It reports version differences and requires authorization before dependency changes.
